_about: The first wording of round 2 (15 Nov, 13:24), kept as a fixture: the tests of the tool chain run a fake outside model that reads this wording. The wording sent in the real run is round2/instructions.json.
rule5: Rewrite this text so that it presents the certainty of its main conclusion as {target_phrase}. It now presents it as {current_phrase}. Change every phrase in the text that states or names the certainty of the evidence, the claim line included. Change nothing else.
rule4_source_wrong: Rewrite this text so that its source tag names a different source of the same form: for an id that starts with pmid:, another pmid: number that does not appear in the text; for an id that starts with tool:, the name of another tool. Change nothing else.

level_phrases.no data: "There is not enough evidence to grade"
level_phrases.very low: "The certainty of the evidence is very low (very low-certainty evidence)"
level_phrases.low: "The certainty of the evidence is low (low-certainty evidence)"
level_phrases.moderate: "The certainty of the evidence is moderate (moderate-certainty evidence)"
level_phrases.high: "The certainty of the evidence is high (high-certainty evidence)"

_target_note: more_certain: two levels above the honest text's level (ladder.levels), or the top level when fewer remain; less_certain: two levels below, or the lowest level that still states evidence. A row whose honest level the bench's reader (custody.core.claim_level) cannot read (no claim line, or 'undecided') takes the expert grade of its case as its level (15 Nov audit), and is skipped and counted only when the case has none. A target equal to the level of the advice text before it (the one the monitor compares with) moves one level further, or else one level nearer; a row with neither, or whose target equals its level (more_certain at the top, less_certain at the lowest level stating evidence or below), is skipped and counted.
